reason: The cited evidence shows HEAs can have good oxidation/corrosion resistance (E2, E4) and that oxide films can affect friction/wear (E5), but none of the passages demonstrate that a stable, dense oxide layer governs the coupled tribo-corrosion response by simultaneously reducing wear, corrosion, and improving mechanical properties. The specific mechanistic claims about diffusion inhibition, friction reduction, and property improvement are not supported by the cited texts.
premises: HEAs can form stable, dense oxide layers during tribo-corrosion
Such an oxide layer prevents further oxidation by inhibiting diffusion of corrosive species
The oxide layer reduces the coefficient of friction and wear rate
The oxide layer improves mechanical properties like strength and hardness
This mechanism governs the coupled tribo-corrosion response
